---
name: plan-authoring
description: Author or revise OpenSlate's restricted declarative video plan from saved shot intents, locked profiles, and registered assets, preserving logical identities, exact keyframe review, and scoped execution reuse.
---

# OpenSlate plan authoring

Produce a validated declaration graph for the current authorized request. The plan is parsed as data; it is never executed as JavaScript. Read [the implemented grammar](references/grammar.md) before authoring source and use [the compiled example](references/example.md) for the exact shape.

Obtain current project revision/head, saved shot IDs, prompts, cues, asset IDs, existing source aliases, and locked profiles through the paged context flow in [the grammar reference](references/grammar.md). For scoped edits, reconstruct all saved canonical source chunks and load existing aliases before changing declarations. Keep established aliases: changing one is not a harmless formatting edit. Never invent permanent node, artifact, approval, or candidate IDs. Shot creation must be applied before source can reference its service-issued IDs.

Use the actual `prepare_change` schema. Its supported change value contains `variant`, `expectedHeadVersion`, and `source`, with optional creative changes and stage proposals. Apply existing-shot pure text changes only when they have no paid-media impact. Until held proposals exist, record edit_field or regenerate_keyframe notes for changes to duration, narration or paid-media inputs. Do not attach proposed design fields that the current schema lacks. Until held proposals exist, record edit_field narration notes for narration changes and do not apply them directly. Collection script/source draft editing requires application-issued narration authority; until held proposals exist, record narration edit choices instead of using the retained `revise_narration_draft` capability. Creative patches cannot update global canonical narration. Use human-accepted canonical cues for executable timing.

Every video must reference a declared exact review and its conditioning image through `p.approvedImage`. That helper declares a dependency; it does not approve an image. Image prompt strings must match current shot image prompts; video and review motion prompts, profile, duration, settings, and frame must agree. Pending media outputs are valid dependencies; unresolved measured timing or human review stays pending at dispatch.

Keep the change focused and retain independent branches. The compiler may reparse the full source while the executor reuses unchanged candidates and outputs. An explicit user-requested additional take is different from continuation: include the existing video node ID in `requestNewTakes` only when current human authority covers it. Do not rename nodes, alter random seeds, or change prompts to bypass grants or force an unrequested variant.

Inspect preparation diagnostics and its compact `impactCounts`/`graphDigest` summary; the full proposal remains stored, not returned. Apply with `{ "preparedId": "the returned identity" }` only while its scope and authority remain current. Inspect receipt context after an uncertain result; stop dependent mutations if evidence is inconclusive, until the application supervisor establishes an authoritative receipt after fencing the old epoch. Refresh/reprepare on actual conflicts; stop old-epoch mutations when authority is revoked. Never release another request's hold or a user pause to advance a graph.

The executor schedules jobs, polls providers, handles trusted technical retries, and reconciles unknown submissions. Do not create per-node agent loops or embed LLM calls in the plan. Report planned work and remaining requirements accurately; inspect current artifact provenance; fixture outputs remain placeholders and successful execution does not establish creative quality.

For explicitly requested recognition of an owned recording or speech from saved narration, use the existing audio tools instead of inventing declarations or grant fields. Audio tools save pending suggestions; only a human press on the audio request route starts paid work. Preserve existing reviewed audio nodes, source bindings and aliases in ordinary plan edits. Do not move a noncanonical owned-recording input into a timeline or another consumer. Visual generation and review are per scene: keyframes first, then actual video. Do not introduce usage allowances or API-key approval steps.
files.plan-authoring/references/grammar.md:
# Implemented planning language 1.0.0

## Load a complete baseline

`read_context` accepts only optional `section` and `offset`: `{}` reads overview; other sections are `shots`, `scenes`, `plan`, `aliases`, `grants`, `receipts`, `narration`, and `audio_operations`. Follow `page.nextOffset` until null for the needed sections. Overview supplies compact identities and locked profiles; full shot intent, prompts, linked cue, and reference records come from `shots`.

Before editing an existing plan, read every `plan` page and concatenate its `source` chunks in order, using the returned offsets (`utf16_characters`, not bytes). Load every `aliases` page and preserve the saved aliases for unchanged operations and reviews. Historical aliases marked `current: false` are not current nodes. Compare `guard.headVersion`, `revisionId`, `activePlanId`, `graphDigest`, `capabilityLockId`, and `domainCursor` across pages; additionally compare `guard.dataDigest` within each section. Restart affected reads if these change. The raw `cursor` tracks audit events and is not a content freshness guard. Never compile a partial chunk or rebuild untouched branches from an overview summary.

Use the current context revision for `baseRevision` and its head version for the change proposal, even when the saved canonical source contains an older base. Replace only the intended declarations and their necessary dependents. Read `grants` to understand unused slots; its authority labels do not grant permission. `receipts` contains outcome identities and summaries, not full proposals or an automatic recovery command.

If the project has no active plan, author source from saved intents and registered assets. Create new shots in a creative-only proposal first, apply it, then read the issued scene/shot IDs before sending source. Existing-shot intent edits and replacement source can be prepared together.

## Declarations

The source is one `definePlan({ baseRevision: "current project revision ID" }, (p) => { ... });` call. The block contains `const` declarations with one binding each and one final return of an operation or operation array. Helpers return typed references, not ordinary runtime objects.

Use finite literal numbers, strings, booleans, null, arrays, plain objects, and earlier local bindings. No imports, exports, arbitrary function calls, loops, branches, assignments, arithmetic, spreads, destructuring, template interpolation, computed properties, type annotations, or arbitrary property access. Write repeated declarations explicitly. Inputs must refer to previously declared operations or registered assets; forward references and cycles fail validation.

All operation and review helpers below take a stable string alias and an options object. The three reference helpers have their own signatures:

| Helper | Exact current inputs |
|---|---|
| `p.asset(id)` | Existing project artifact ID; no paths or URLs |
| `p.shot(id)` | Existing shot ID, current shot revision ID, or `id@revision`; prefer the saved stable ID |
| `p.approvedImage(image, review)` | Image reference and a review declaring that exact image |
| `p.image(alias, options)` | Required `profile`, `prompt`; optional `intent`, `references`, `width`, `height`, `settings` |
| `p.humanReview(alias, options)` | Required `shots` array; each member requires `intent`, `keyframe`, `videoProfile`, `motionPrompt`, `seconds`; optional `settings` |
| `p.video(alias, options)` | Required `intent`, `profile`, `firstFrame`, `prompt`, `seconds`; optional `settings` |
| `p.speech(alias, options)` | Required `profile`, `text`, `voice`; optional `instructions`, `settings` |
| `p.transcription(alias, options)` | Required `profile`, `audio`; optional `language`, `timing` (`segment`, `word`, `none`), `settings` |
| `p.timeline(alias, options)` | Required nonempty ordered `takes`; optional `narration`, `transition` (`cut`), `cueRange` (known cue or scene ID) |
| `p.render(alias, options)` | Required `timeline` operation; optional `width`, `height`, `format` (`mp4`) |

Image references preserve array order. Include every registered reference required by shot intent. Image dimensions default to 1024 square; provided dimensions must be even integers from 16 to 8192. An image linked to a shot uses its exact saved image prompt.

The video's `firstFrame` must be `p.approvedImage(...)`, never a bare image. The review and video must match shot, frame, locked profile/revision, prompt, duration, and settings. Video seconds must be whole numbers within the configured profile bounds; the compiler requires enough source frames for the planned shot. An explicit `shot.narration.mode=none` with no cue uses planned visual duration. For compact narration with application-issued within-shot timing, accepted measured voiceover may be shorter than the planned visual slot. Legacy audio-led timing still requires accepted measured cue duration and desired shot frames to agree. In every mode the requested video must cover the planned shot frames. The application derives readiness; model-authored timing mode or acceptance fields are unavailable. Do not turn this implementation constraint into a false claim about general vendor capabilities.

Default demonstration profiles are `fake-image-v1`, `fake-video-v1`, `fake-speech-v1`, and `fake-transcription-v1`; production projects may pin explicit provider profiles. Use only profiles supplied by the actual capability lock. Changing to a vendor's model name does not install an adapter. Profile-specific `settings` are plain JSON data; they cannot register code or add unsupported operations.

Timeline take order is edit order, not a requirement to generate shots serially. Narration takes an audio reference. The initial frame rate is 30 fps; the project duration ceiling is 10800 frames. Physical rendering uses verified owned media and current canonical audio placements; short accepted compact voiceover remains inside its planned visual slot. Render dimensions default to 1280×720 and must be even integers within 16–8192.

Operation outputs are image→`image`, video→`video`, speech→`audio`, transcription→`cues`, timeline→`timeline`, render→`video`. These ports are compiler output metadata, not properties to read in source. Pass the operation reference itself to the next helper.

Read diagnostics literally: resolve a missing reference, stale prompt, review mismatch, or unsupported capability. A gate declaration or successful compilation cannot supply human keyframe/video review. A malformed proposal can be corrected within the request; no-progress reassessment must stop instead of creating an autonomous loop.

## Reviewed audio operations

New requested recording transcription and saved-section speech use the existing audio tools, as pending suggestions; only an explicit human press starts paid work. Preserve their existing declarations exactly when retaining the current plan. A saved `p.transcriptionInput(id)` reference belongs only to its exact transcription consumer; do not invent a binding, change its consumer, strip its application linkage or pass its recording into a timeline. Matching bytes do not create ownership or content acceptance. A speech declaration also cannot borrow another operation's source or scope.

The unchanged V4 JSON schema for creative shot creation/update accepts optional `narration: {mode: "undecided" | "none" | "generated" | "uploaded", text: string, voice: "stock" | "personal"}`. This saves writing intent only. Use `reauthorPrompts: true` for updates and preserve unaffected visual fields. Never submit `narrationPending`, `narrationTimingMode`, cue acceptance or grant fields. An explicit none choice clears only that shot’s cue through the application.

name: production
description: Develop or revise an OpenSlate narrated video from the current brief, assets, narration choices, and shot evidence; identify missing decisions and guide human review within the requested scope.

# OpenSlate production

Turn the user's current request into useful scoped creative work. Read the application context for settled decisions, allowed scope, current revisions, existing media, and pending requirements. Choose the relevant stages; a shot edit does not restart intake or the whole film. Several stages can be addressed in one proposal. The application derives mandatory checks from the actual changes, so a stage label never grants permission or bypasses a requirement.

Read [notes and human decisions](references/notes.md) before any mutation. Read [the current contract](references/current-contract.md) before forming a tool payload. It explains paged context, source chunks, freshness guards, and the compact preparation result. Use `read_context` and `inspect_artifact` for missing evidence, `record_notes` for narration edit choices, `revise_narration_draft` remains a compatibility capability; until held proposals exist, use note choices for narration changes, `prepare_change` for a creative or plan proposal, and `apply_change` for the returned prepared-change identity. Use `prepare_recording_transcription` for requested recognition of an existing owned recording and `prepare_narration_speech` for requested speech from one exact saved narration section. The application saves these as pending suggestions until a human presses the audio action; their returned identities are not IDs accepted by `apply_change`. Narration drafts remain reversible and returned audio does not adopt or accept itself. Preserve operation identity when inspecting a lost response. Do not invent actor, approval, grant, or completion fields. A skill supplies guidance; the application owns authority and state.

Use [audio operations](references/audio-proposals.md) for explicitly requested recognition or speech. Read `audio_operations` for current profiles, recordings and outcomes. Configured provider credentials need no separate approval or usage allowance. Report a real missing key, unsupported input or disabled route as setup information; do not ask the user to approve a key or authorize narration guidance.

Use [narration decisions](references/narration.md) when audio or script coverage is uncertain, and [continuity and review](references/continuity-review.md) for assets, shot edits, or visual feedback. Load only the stage prompts needed for this request:

| Stage | Prompt reference | Read when |
|---|---|---|
| `intake` | [production/intake@1](references/stages/intake.md) | Interpreting a brief or new attachments |
| `story` | [production/story@1](references/stages/story.md) | Developing beats and visual direction |
| `scene_plan` | [production/scene_plan@1](references/stages/scene_plan.md) | Organizing scene purposes and coverage |
| `shot_plan` | [production/shot_plan@1](references/stages/shot_plan.md) | Creating or revising shot intent and prompts |
| `narration` | [production/narration@1](references/stages/narration.md) | Choosing script and audio work |
| `storyboard` | [production/storyboard@1](references/stages/storyboard.md) | Preparing conditioning images for review |
| `video` | [production/video@1](references/stages/video.md) | Planning reviewed video work or a requested take |
| `assembly` | [production/assembly@1](references/stages/assembly.md) | Planning cuts, narration placement, and previews |
| `review` | [production/review@1](references/stages/review.md) | Explaining visible results and receiving human decisions |

Ask for missing information when it changes the creative result or a required choice. Do not repeat settled questions or turn aesthetic concerns into hard blockers. Record concise advisory gaps; let service diagnostics identify enforced requirements. Continue independent drafting when feasible.

Each scene has two generation decisions: create keyframes from its direction, then inspect the exact returned frames with their motion, duration, model and settings before starting video. Use each scene's green actions for those decisions. Returned clips are available to inspect; a green completion status means current media is saved, not that quality was accepted. Do not add a post-generation acceptance gate, cost review, usage allowance or API-key approval. An additional creative take still requires the user's scoped request. Never regenerate automatically to improve quality, label an aesthetic miss a technical failure, or resubmit uncertain work. The executor owns trusted technical retries and reconciliation.

Use `plan-authoring` when producing executable declarations. Let deterministic media progress continue without another reasoning turn. After applying, report the concrete change, preserved work, and remaining user decision or system requirement. Current fixture artifacts must be described as fake; a successful tool receipt is not proof of artistic quality or a completed real film.

Current V6 policy: read references/notes.md. Record one point per note and respect resolved decisions. Until held proposals exist, do not apply duration, narration or paid-media-invalidating changes; offer typed human edit/regenerate choices. Never judge unseen pictures. Audio tools save pending suggestions; only a human press starts paid work.

# Audio suggestions

Read narration and audio_operations for exact saved section or owned recording identities, supported profiles and outcomes. prepare_narration_speech and prepare_recording_transcription save pending suggestions only. They never publish paid work. A person presses the existing audio action to generate. Do not pass suggestion IDs to apply_change or publish speech/transcription in a plan. No separate spending approval or usage allowance is needed. Returned media and transcripts never attach, adopt or accept themselves. Unknown outcomes retain their original operation identity; never resubmit blindly.
# Continuity and human review

For each affected shot, compare the relevant neighboring shots and shared references. Track subject identity, product details, wardrobe, setting, time of day, lighting direction, screen direction, camera distance, and action progression only where they matter. Preserve established choices; propose a changed continuity rule explicitly instead of letting prompts drift independently.

Separate the image prompt's composition and visible subject from the video's intended motion. Prefer a clear action and camera move that fit the clip duration. Carry approved product or character references through the supported reference inputs. Do not invent reference images or claim that text alone guarantees identity consistency.

Every video is conditioned on the exact image reviewed by the human. A frame needs cropping, replacement, or changed settings before approval, not an invisible alteration afterward. Review describes the frame together with motion, duration, and profile; an image-only “looks good” is not automatically an approval of a different generation setup. The human decision channel records the exact displayed subset. Neither a prompt nor `p.approvedImage` records that decision.

When a close-up would outdate paid media, record a typed edit or regeneration note instead of applying it. Retain neighboring shots' settled choices. Present any continuity consequence. Keep previous takes in history; only compatible current results should enter the new draft. A late result from the replaced candidate remains evidence, not an instruction to restore the old choice.

Treat aesthetic criticism as creative feedback. Interpret the requested change and its scope, then use the application's scene controls for an additional requested take. Do not launch a self-directed “improve until good” loop. A lost response is unresolved work, and a technically valid ugly clip is not a technical failure. Trusted retry classification, current-input admission and recovery are executor responsibilities.

If image inspection is unavailable to the active model, describe only verified metadata and request human visual judgment. Never report unseen content as checked. When current artifact evidence marks a preview as a fixture, describe it as placeholder footage. Do not infer all outputs are fixtures or all are real from a provider choice.

Current V6 policy: read references/notes.md. Record one point per note and respect resolved decisions. Until held proposals exist, do not apply duration, narration or paid-media-invalidating changes; offer typed human edit/regenerate choices. Never judge unseen pictures. Audio tools save pending suggestions; only a human press starts paid work.

# Current contract

Guidance package `6.0.0`, tool contract `5.0.0`, workflow and planning contracts `1.0.0`. Nine tools include record_notes. Audio preparation tools save pending suggestions only; a person presses the existing request action to start paid speech or transcription. No separate spending approval or allowance is required. Each scene has two human generation decisions: create keyframes, then review exact returned frames and the actual video recipe before video generation. Notes never authorize generation. Held proposals are unavailable. Read notes.md for when to note, ask or apply and how to respect settled decisions.

## Reading the current state

Call `read_context` with `{}` for the first overview, or `{ "section": "shots", "offset": 0 }` for a specific page. Supported sections are `overview`, `shots`, `scenes`, `plan`, `aliases`, `grants`, `receipts`, `narration`, `audio_operations`, and `notes`. Follow the returned `page.nextOffset` until null for the collections needed by the task. Do not infer that the first page is the full project. Overview contains compact shot/scene identities, messages, workflow and work summaries, request scope, and locked profiles; read `shots` and `scenes` for complete intent records.

Keep pages from the same state: compare `guard.headVersion`, `revisionId`, `activePlanId`, `graphDigest`, `capabilityLockId`, and `domainCursor` across reads; compare `guard.dataDigest` within the same section. If these change, refresh the affected context and restart its pagination. The raw `cursor` is an event-stream position and changes for tool audit events; do not use it as the pagination guard. A size error is explicit missing context, never permission to assume the omitted content.

For an existing-plan edit, load all `plan` pages and concatenate each returned `source` in offset order. These are chunks of the saved **canonical source**, not complete independent programs. The offset unit is `utf16_characters`; always use `page.nextOffset` instead of calculating a byte offset. Retain matching plan/source identities across chunks and load all `aliases` pages to preserve existing node and review identities. An alias with `current: false` is historical, not evidence of a current operation. Read the affected complete shot intents and preserve untouched branches from the saved source. If `activePlanId` is null, no existing executable plan has been supplied.

Use `grants` to inspect unused slots and their recorded authority relationship. This is information, not new authorization; the service rechecks current request, scope, origin, and consumption. `receipts` returns compact command/tool identities and digests for reviewing earlier outcomes, not full stored proposals. If a tool outcome is unresolved, inspect available application evidence and stop dependent mutations when the result cannot be established; the application supervisor can reconcile authoritative receipts after fencing the old epoch, but the model cannot force replay. Do not issue a fresh creative interpretation or new candidate to recover a lost response.

## Preparing and applying a change

The application accepts a `ChangeProposal` with `variant` equal to `workflow`, `project`, or `plan`, and the current integer `expectedHeadVersion`. Optional fields are `stages`, `creative`, `source`, and `requestNewTakes`. At least one stage proposal, creative patch, or source is required. The tool transport may wrap this value: use the exposed schema rather than guessing a call signature.

A stage proposal has `stageId`, an existing `scopeId`, a concise `reason`, and optional `gaps: [{ key, message }]`. Use stable gap keys within the scope. Do not send the proposed design's `mode`, `basedOn`, completion status, severity, or approval fields: they are absent from the implemented schema. The service determines contract coverage even for project-only and plan-only inputs.

Supported creative fields:

- `brief` and `story`. Global canonical `narrationScript` and `narrationSource` fields remain unavailable. Compact shot writing is supported through the narration intent field described below.
- `createScenes: [{ key, purpose }]` and `updateScenes: [{ id, purpose }]`.
- `createShots`: each entry supplies `key`, `sceneId`, `purpose`, `action`, `framing`, `motion`, integer `desiredFrames`, `imagePrompt`, `videoPrompt`, `referenceArtifactIds`, and `cueId` (existing cue ID or null). A scene's creation key can be used within the same creative patch; the application allocates permanent IDs.
- `updateShots`: existing `id` plus changed purpose/action/framing/motion/duration/prompts, optional compact `narration` intent and `reauthorPrompts: true`. Deliberately rewrite or reconfirm the prompts against the changed intent before setting that flag. Updating references or cue IDs is not supported by this patch shape.

Do not send `promptIntent` hashes, project/shot revisions, audio acceptance, measured cue times, or grant records as creative patch fields. The service owns these records and validates links. Creating shots and referring to their not-yet-issued IDs in executable source in the same proposal is unsupported: apply the creative draft, read its saved IDs, then author the plan. The schema permits existing-shot edits and replacement source atomically, but V6 only applies pure text changes without paid-media impact. Until held proposals exist, duration, narration and paid-media-invalidating changes must be recorded as typed human choices instead.

`prepare_change` returns a compact result: `id`/`preparedId`, `proposalDigest`, `baseVersion`, `semanticChange`, `graphDigest`, `impactCounts`, and `stageCount`. The full proposal, next project, and compiled graph remain stored in the application; do not expect them in the response. Check the returned summary and any diagnostics, then call `apply_change` with `{ "preparedId": "the returned identity" }`. A successful preparation does not apply the draft or approve media. After applying, refresh the relevant context pages; never guess newly allocated IDs from creation keys.

`requestNewTakes` contains existing video **node IDs**, not shot IDs or source aliases, and requires source in the same proposal. Use it only for a requested additional take covered by human authority. Matching inputs can reuse valid frame approval; they must not silently substitute a cached take for the requested new candidate.

On a revision conflict, refresh the affected state and reprepare. On revoked authority, stop mutations under that request. Holds and global pause remain application controls: do not clear them as a planning shortcut. A project-only edit can leave affected execution held until a compatible plan is applied. A new human message may explicitly continue an older edit; the model cannot fabricate that continuation.

Creative/plan preparation has no paid effects. Audio tools save pending suggestions only; a human press is required before the executor starts paid work. Polling, generation attempts and uncertain submissions belong to that executor. Resolve missing current inputs, required keyframe review or setup from application evidence; never invent another identity or stage label to bypass a requirement. Usage allowances and API-key approval are absent from the current user flow.


## Notes and scoped writing

Read notes.md before choosing a mutation. The supported schema is not permission to apply duration, narration or paid-media-invalidating changes directly. Record an edit_field or regenerate_keyframe choice until held proposals exist. Respect existing narration session scopes and settled text/audio/timing decisions. Never widen an ordinary shot request to the global narration collection.

# Narration decisions

First determine what the user already supplied: final recording, partial recording, approved script, rough text, or only an idea. Inspect registered evidence when available. Treat a filename, attachment mention, desired duration, or language-model estimate as insufficient evidence of measured audio timing.

For a final recording, preserve its words and performance unless the user requests changes. Establish what it covers and what must appear visually. For an approved script without audio, preserve the wording and establish voice/language/pronunciation choices that matter before proposing speech. For rough notes, draft a coherent script tied to the intended audience and duration. For partial material, identify the missing passages without replacing accepted passages or pretending the whole narration is ready.

Ask the smallest useful question: for example, whether a missing passage should be recorded by the user or generated. Reuse settled voice, tone, and source decisions. An approximate reading duration can inform planning but must stay labeled as an estimate.

Read the `narration` context section to distinguish saved notes/outlines/drafts, script acceptance, bound audio, measured cues and independent human audio/timing acceptance. Include unbound recordings in the inventory. A mentioned upload or a measured recording descriptor is not a known transcript. If recognition is requested and an owned recording is available, read audio_operations and prepare its exact transcription proposal. An independent recording needs no script or section. Otherwise ask for missing words or draft a separate script; never claim to have heard an uninspected file.

For narration changes, record a note with an edit_field narration choice until held proposals exist. Do not apply narration changes directly. Preserve settled fields and IDs. A source preference does not attach audio, buy speech, or mark anything accepted.

A changed section clears its script/audio/timing acceptance and selected cue; changing source also detaches its recording candidate. Unchanged sections and history survive. Tell the user which sections need exact review. The human uses narration controls to upload/attach recordings, set trims/placement, accept script/audio/timing and review/apply the canonical change. Agent tools do not perform those actions. Ask the smallest useful question about a genuine missing choice and keep independent story work moving.

For application-locked video, an explicit No narration shot uses its planned visual duration with no cue. A compact accepted voiceover may be shorter than the planned shot when the application marks within-shot timing; its exact accepted audio is placed inside that planned duration. Legacy audio-led timing still requires accepted measured cue duration, desired shot frames and requested video frames to agree. Review can precede final readiness; dispatch cannot. At 30 fps, six seconds is 180 frames. Approximate reading duration is only an estimate. Do not change planned visual duration just because a compact voiceover is short.

Pure placement changes may preserve visual media when consumed meaning and relative timing stay equivalent. Changed words or pacing require independent audio review; an application-marked within-shot voiceover preserves its visual recipe when the planned shot duration stays the same. Changed shot duration requires fresh relevant planning and possibly review. Keep exact audio/placement lineage for assembly; never claim that an unchanged visual prompt proves narration compatibility.

Use the existing audio tools for explicitly requested recognition or speech. See [audio operations](audio-proposals.md). Audio tools save pending suggestions; only an explicit human press starts paid work; returned media or words do not attach, adopt or accept themselves.

Current V6 policy: read references/notes.md. Record one point per note and respect resolved decisions. Until held proposals exist, do not apply duration, narration or paid-media-invalidating changes; offer typed human edit/regenerate choices. Never judge unseen pictures. Audio tools save pending suggestions; only a human press starts paid work.
files.production/references/notes.md:
# Notes and human decisions

Read the notes context before raising a point. Never re-raise a resolved note or a settled human decision; stale notes describe old inputs, not new blockers.

Use record_notes for a concrete observation or recommendation anchored to existing shot IDs (or their scene). Keep one point per note, at most six notes per call. Use the app-assigned letters returned by the tool; do not invent letters or action labels. Each blocking note must offer an accept choice that keeps the current result. Choice labels for edits and regeneration come from typed actions rendered by the app.

Ask a concise question when required information is missing, rather than recording an invented conclusion. Apply directly only pure text changes that do not outdate paid media. Changes to duration or narration, or changes that would outdate paid media, belong in held proposals once that facility exists. Held proposals and propose_change are unavailable in this catalog: record an edit_field or regenerate_keyframe choice instead and let the person perform it. Do not use prepare/apply to bypass this boundary. Future proposals contain one change each.

Never judge a picture you were not shown. A visual observation requires exact attachedKeyframes evidence; artifact metadata, a prompt, or a frame-view receipt is not visual access. Without images, discuss writing or ask the person to inspect the picture. Do not supply seenKeyframe unless it is present in attachedKeyframes.

Paid choices are always pressed by a person through the existing priced generation/audio action. Notes never start generation. A person may keep the result, press regeneration, edit the field, or reply. The app resolves the note with the saved human action, and stales it when anchored shot revisions or seen frame hashes change. A resolution is not new authority to edit or spend.

# production/assembly@1

Choose the intended take sequence and narration relationship from the current plan and usable evidence. Preserve deliberate existing selections. Identify unresolved takes or timing instead of silently substituting whichever artifact finished last.

The implemented planning language supports ordered takes, optional narration input, cuts, an optional known cue/scene range, and an MP4 render declaration. It does not provide a full editor, overlays, transitions beyond cuts, or additional editor helpers. Verified owned media can be rendered through the application’s local pipeline. Describe those requests as future work or unresolved choices rather than inventing helpers.

Use `plan-authoring` for the supported timeline and render declarations. Their dependencies may be pending at preparation. Deterministic execution and equivalent-result caching need no per-shot reasoning loop. Distinguish planned duration and the selected timeline from a stale or one-second fake preview; a fixture render is not an export-ready long video.
files.production/references/stages/intake.md:
# production/intake@1

Interpret the current request in the context of the saved project. Identify its output, audience, approximate duration, aspect or delivery format, subject constraints, and supplied assets only as far as needed to start useful work. Distinguish a new film from an edit or review of existing work.

Preserve explicit decisions and existing final material. Inspect available evidence instead of interviewing the user again. Propose a concise `brief` change when appropriate. Raise advisory gaps for choices that materially affect the next creative step; unknown implementation support should be described plainly.

Do not invent IDs for attachments or import unregistered paths into a plan. Develop the creative plan, then use each scene's generation and media-review controls for the next visual step. Do not ask for a separate API-key or usage approval. Return supported stage proposals and useful draft content in one bounded proposal when possible.
files.production/references/stages/narration.m:
# production/narration@1

Use the [narration decision guide](../narration.md) to distinguish recordings, approved scripts, drafts, and missing passages. For narration changes, record an edit_field narration note and wait for the human edit until held proposals exist. Do not apply narration changes directly. Retain unrelated section IDs and accepted choices. Preserve accepted material and ask for the decision needed to fill a real gap.

For explicitly requested speech or transcription, use the existing audio tools with current saved recording or section identities; see [audio operations](../audio-proposals.md). The tools save pending suggestions only. An explicit human press on the existing audio route starts paid work; no separate spending approval is needed. Describe fixture outputs as fixtures, and inspect current provenance before claiming an actual recording or recognized result. Neither establishes accepted measured cues.

Keep narration coverage and readiness separate. A script can be creatively settled while audio work is pending. An uploaded filename can be known while probing is unavailable. Save those distinctions as concise gaps and proceed with independent creative work rather than fabricating timing or blocking every scene.
files.production/references/stages/review.md:
# production/review@1

Summarize the exact displayed scope and its intended behavior. For keyframes, show which shot, image, motion, duration, and profile the decision covers. For finished clips, separate technical availability from continuity, pacing, identity, and other creative observations supported by actual inspection.

Let the trusted human decision channel record approval of the displayed subset. Ambiguous, conditional, negative, or quoted language is not blanket approval. Missing visual capability requires human inspection, not invented observations.

Interpret feedback as a scoped change: what should improve, which shot or scene it affects, and which existing choices remain relevant. Preserve prior takes. Request or use the existing human authority for a specific additional candidate; do not repeatedly regenerate until your own quality judgment is satisfied. Return the current review requirement or focused proposal without marking stages complete yourself.

Current V6 policy: read references/notes.md. Record one point per note and respect resolved decisions. Until held proposals exist, do not apply duration, narration or paid-media-invalidating changes; offer typed human edit/regenerate choices. Never judge unseen pictures. Audio tools save pending suggestions; only a human press starts paid work.
# production/scene_plan@1

Group the relevant story beats or narration passages into scenes with distinct purposes. Consider transitions, location continuity, available references, and whether the coverage fits the intended duration. Reuse existing scene IDs when revising their purposes.

The current scene patch records `purpose` and service-issued identity. It has no dedicated ordering, timing, or narration-range fields. Include concise planning intent in the purpose when useful; let supported shot and timeline declarations express the actual execution order. Do not add speculative schema fields.

Scene drafting and narration development may proceed together. Keep provisional duration assumptions explicit. A scene purpose change may affect several shots; identify that impact without replacing unrelated scenes or treating scene order as a mandatory generation dependency.
files.production/references/stages/shot_plan.m:
# production/shot_plan@1

Specify what each requested shot communicates, the visible action, framing, camera or subject motion, references, and intended duration. Make neighboring shots complementary rather than repeated descriptions. Use settled scene purposes and narration meaning as constraints.

Create shots through the supported creative patch and then read their saved IDs before writing executable source. For an existing shot, preserve its ID. Reauthor or deliberately reconfirm both prompts against changed intent and set `reauthorPrompts: true`; never change the framing while silently keeping a contradictory old prompt.

A planned visual duration is explicit. No narration uses it directly; accepted compact voiceover fits inside that visual slot unless the human explicitly chooses audio-led duration. The current source uses seconds while shot intent uses integer frames at 30 fps. Review and video must use the same effective settings. For existing shots, record notes for changes to duration, narration or paid-media inputs until held proposals exist. Apply only pure text edits without media impact.

# production/story@1

Develop a clear progression from the settled brief or narration: what the viewer understands first, what develops, and what the ending resolves or asks them to do. Give each beat a visible purpose. Keep claims consistent with supplied facts; do not invent product promises for dramatic effect.

Use the supported `story` text to state the beats, emotional direction, and recurring visual idea. Match ambition to the duration and available assets. If a final narration already establishes the story, adapt its visual treatment rather than replacing its wording.

Draft through nonessential uncertainty with stated assumptions. Ask about a material conflict between the user's goals. A structured story draft is useful evidence, not automatically an accepted screenplay or a requirement to run every earlier stage again.
# production/storyboard@1

Prepare one conditioning image per shot requiring video, using the current shot intent and registered references. A usable imported frame may be reused after the application's normalization and review requirements; an existing frame's mere presence does not imply approval.

Choose composition, subject visibility, lighting, and framing that support the planned movement. Keep references and prompts consistent with adjacent shots. Use the plan-authoring grammar to declare image work and exact review membership. A generated frame may be a future symbolic input while the plan is prepared.

Present the actual resulting frame and intended motion/duration for human review. Do not perform hidden image changes after approval or create variants merely because you dislike the result. Pending narration timing may allow image preparation; it does not waive later video readiness checks.

# production/video@1

Translate settled shot motion into a supported video declaration using its exact conditioning frame and matching review recipe. Read the locked profile and existing work; never infer an available vendor adapter from a model name mentioned in conversation.

Video waits for exact human keyframe/motion/video-recipe review, application-derived narration readiness, a current requested candidate and unpaused configured dispatch. The scene's second generation action starts the requested work; no separate usage/spending allowance is needed. An explicit No narration choice with no cue uses its planned duration. An accepted compact within-shot voiceover may be shorter than the planned shot; legacy audio-led timing still requires cue/shot duration agreement. The requested video must cover the planned shot frames. A planned video can remain symbolic while those requirements are pending. Do not replace the video with text-to-video or remove its review dependency to make it run. Returned clips remain available for inspection without another acceptance gate; saved output is not evidence of artistic quality.

For an explicit additional take, use the current video node ID in `requestNewTakes` with a current source proposal and scoped human authority. Preserve unchanged approval when the application validates it. For ordinary continuation, reuse compatible work. Unknown submissions and technical retries stay with the executor; quality regeneration always needs the user's request.

Current V6 policy: read references/notes.md. Record one point per note and respect resolved decisions. Until held proposals exist, do not apply duration, narration or paid-media-invalidating changes; offer typed human edit/regenerate choices. Never judge unseen pictures.
